A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same THESEUS research work. Their complete main text, Appendices A–G, equations, tables and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original vision and language transfer experiments, summarization results, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices E and G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including transfer accuracies, summarization scores and alignment ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1 and the depth-interpolation procedure in Section 4.4 are unchanged. The added software-framework attribution does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight vision datasets, five natural-language inference datasets and CNN/DailyMail summarization task, with unchanged transfer scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged, including TransFusion, GradFix, pseudo-inverse variants and feature-alignment baselines. The added citations do not introduce experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The B-shot and K-shot protocols, calibration budgets, model configurations, validation-based update scaling, training settings and language evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The update-scaling sensitivity, warm-start, activation-alignment, sequence-interpolation and transport-operator analyses are retained unchanged in Sections 4.5–4.7 and Appendices E and G.

E5.justification: Run/seed information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. No uncertainty estimates, repeated-run disclosures or significance analyses are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11 and Figures 2–5 retain the same results. For example, Table 1 reports the same 69.08% THESEUS average at B=20 and 58.76% target zero-shot average in both versions.

T1.justification: The functional-matching definitions, orthogonality assumptions, transport and norm derivations, complexity analysis and appendix mathematical formulations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free functional transport, geometric preservation, heterogeneous-model transfer and fine-tuning initialization.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same mechanism explanations and qualifications concerning heuristic depth alignment, validation-based scaling and inherited source-update limitations. The impact discussion is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly states that the code is implemented in the merge-and-rebase framework and cites Panariello et al. (2026). This adds explicit implementation attribution; the code URL and technical settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds a formal Panariello et al. (2026) framework reference and a Sommariva et al. (2026) citation for update scaling. Sommariva replaces a local Rinaldi et al. (2025) citation, while Rinaldi remains cited elsewhere. Research positioning is otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short implementation-framework sentence and Villanova funding acknowledgment, and updates citations and the version stamp. The scientific exposition, terminology and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additions cause limited column and page-break reflow in the acknowledgments, references and appendices. All figures and tables retain their displays, captions and locations.

improvement.justification: v3 adds bibliographic and implementation attribution plus funding credit, but v2 already supplied the same code link. With unchanged methods, proofs, experiments, results and limitations, these limited documentation refinements do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
